angle: How did a print that cost two bowls of noodles become the world's most famous wave?
hooks: Van Gogh said this wave has claws.
The world's most famous wave began as a cheap souvenir.

painting.title: The Great Wave off Kanagawa
painting.museum: Impressions in the Met, the British Museum and others

script.text: This wave once cost about two bowls of noodles.
In 2023, one copy sold for 2.76 million dollars.
script.say: In twenty twenty-three, one copy sold for two point seven six million dollars.

script.text: So how does a cheap print become the world's most famous wave?
It starts with a new blue from China that never faded.
The series sold so well that the publisher added ten more views.
But a hit print wore out its own woodblocks.
Thousands were pulled, each one blurring the carved lines a little more.
That's why crisp early copies are so rare, and so fought over.
But its fame was made far from Japan.
In 1888, Van Gogh wrote to his brother that its waves are claws, and the boat is caught.
script.say: In eighteen eighty-eight, Van Gogh wrote to his brother that its waves are claws, and the boat is caught.

script.text: A year later he painted Starry Night, and one expert sees this wave in its sky.
Yet Hokusai thought he had barely started.
He wrote that nothing he drew before seventy was worth noticing.
So a new blue, worn woodblocks and Van Gogh's Europe made a cheap print priceless.
Its maker died at eighty-nine, asking for five more years to become a real artist.
